`icd10_diag1`, `icd10_diag2`, and `icd10_diag3` are currently split from `mod_psiq_dsm_iv`. They are DSM-IV aliases until the producing code is corrected.
The R Cox path censors readmission when death time is <= readmission time. March Python preprocessing uses a strict < comparison. Exact ties therefore differ.
`ed_attainment_corr` prevents implausible within-person decreases, but the filled object is not joined back. Missing education is not imputed in the executed final data.
`porc_pobr` uses commune income poverty through 2021 and 2022 multidimensional poverty afterward, so its meaning changes across periods.
DeepSurv and XGBoost use a shared 56-feature matrix. Twelve ordered fields are integer-scored, while Cox reconstructs 26 corresponding dummy columns.
`tr_outcome_other` is created and then all such rows are excluded. The rule-violation dummy remains a neural/boosting predictor but becomes a Cox stratum.
DeepSurv2's corrected dual-event logic supersedes older DeepSurv tuning blocks that used the mortality follow-up time for readmission.
An early split export uses 0-based `row_id`; the later R-compatible file overwrites it with 1-based `row_id` and additional columns.
R creates `center_id` as a factor and later applies `as.numeric()`, yielding internal factor codes that may not equal the original center values.
